headline: Asia's chip markets slide into Nvidia week
tone: Asia opened the week by selling the AI supply chain.
body: Asia opened the week by selling the AI supply chain. Taiwan and Korea took the brunt, Tokyo followed, while Hong Kong edged up and mainland China barely moved, so this is a chip trade unwinding rather than a regional rout. Nasdaq futures are softer than the S&P, which points the same way.

Nvidia's results on Tuesday night are now the week's test for the whole theme. Washington plans to name Nvidia and other AI firms national champions, which offers political cover but does not answer the leadership questions hanging over the company.

Iran struck Bahrain overnight, widening the Gulf hostilities beyond the Houthi attacks on Riyadh covered on Sunday. Crude barely reacted, a sign the market still sees no hit to Gulf supply; a strike on export infrastructure would change that quickly.

China's October activity data came in weaker than expected, adding to the case for faster budget spending in Beijing. Nordic power jumped back into the working week, with Finland and the northern Swedish zones rising from very low Sunday levels.

views.text: Last week's Asian bounce has been handed back where it was strongest, which says investors are cutting AI exposure before Nvidia reports rather than waiting for the numbers. Weak Chinese data adds a growth worry on top. Watch whether Europe's open and the US cash session follow Asia's chip names or treat this as a pre-earnings shakeout.

Sunday's collapse was a weekend and wind effect, and the Monday rebound puts the whole region back in its November pattern: the south priced off Germany, the north cheap. November has been less windy than October, with hydro making up the gap, which draws on reservoirs heading into winter. More nuclear back online is the main thing holding Finland and SE3 below the continental level.
